title: rf positioning
description:
The current public framing sells rf as recovery ("it finds files rg hid"), which
reads as a more aggressive grep and invites the "just add ripgrep flags" rebuttal.
The stronger, approved position leads with the felt danger and resolves it with the
control surface. This epic produces the repositioned public copy; it is kept separate
from the contract reconciliation so copy work and accuracy work do not block each
other, but the crate publish depends on the copy landing so both reach crates.io in
one version.

Approved positioning hierarchy: (1) lead with the scar — a search can miss most
matches and still exit 0, and the blind spot multiplies the moment it is piped with
file-find, history, or structural search; (2) name the audience in the next breath —
this is for when a program acts on the result, while interactive use of the
underlying tools stays fine; (3) the control surface — one envelope, typed exits,
`capabilities`, provenance, paging cursors, path-envelope chaining; (4) recovery
examples as proof, not headline; (5) rf as a worked example of applying agent-first
control-surface design to a mature, human-first CLI, sized honestly (one clean-tool
cluster demonstrated; broader generality not yet proven). Tagline: "Search results
that agents can inspect, explain, and safely continue from."
acceptance_criteria:
- The public copy follows the approved hierarchy, scar first.
- The copy keeps claims at product level and passes the internal-identifier leak gate
  on every surface it touches.

title: Documentation and contract reconciliation
description:
The rf executable, the crate docs (README and CHANGELOG), and the docs site at
rgfind.dev have drifted apart. Two independent prose doc trees both describe an
older contract than the one the binary actually ships, in places contradicting
each other and the executable. This epic reconciles every public documentation
surface with the binary's real contract, surface by surface, and adds a guardrail
so the drift cannot silently return.

Verified binary contract (the reconciliation target): verbs are `capabilities`,
`conformance`, `content`, `doctor`, `find`, and `robot-docs guide`; exit codes are
0 (success), 1 (no match), 3 (environment/retryable), 5 (changed-snapshot
conflict), 6 (internal); there are 11 error codes; `contract_version` is 2; every
command returns one JSON envelope with seven keys — `ok`, `tool_version`, `data`,
`meta`, `warnings`, `commands`, `errors` — where `data` is `null` on failure and
`[]` on a successful empty result; `content` reports `surfaced_by` in
{default, vcs_ignore, hidden, binary, case, encoding_utf16}; `find` reports `stage`
in {found, fd_name, fd_hidden, fd_ignore, fd_filter, rg_binary, git_deleted,
ast_structural}.

Capture and coverage are split by surface so the live-site corrections proceed
immediately and do not wait on the crate release path. crates.io is write-once:
a published release's README and metadata cannot be edited without a version bump,
and `cargo publish` packages the working tree at publish time.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every public documentation surface (site pages and crate README/CHANGELOG) states
  only values that equal the captured capability fixture for the artifact that
  surface ships with.
- A guardrail fails the build on a seeded drift in any registered contract fact and
  passes on a reconciled tree, per tree.
- No internal tooling identifiers leak into any public surface.

Get public text right before the next publish.","Capture and coverage are split by surface so the live-site corrections proceed now and do not wait on the crate release path."]}

title: Pin published-crate artifact and site fixture
description:
The site documents the currently published crate, so the site's source of truth
must be a captured, committed snapshot of that published artifact's contract — not
the working tree and not prose. Without a pinned fixture, every downstream site
edit would diff against a moving target.
design:
Install the published crate cleanly into a temporary root and capture
`rf capabilities --json` verbatim. Commit it as the site capability fixture
(`capabilities.site.json`). Record the package version, the source revision where
available, and the capture's content hash alongside it. Write a one-paragraph note
naming which public surfaces target this artifact (the site does).
acceptance_criteria:
- `capabilities.site.json` is committed with version, revision, and content hash.
- A short site-target mapping paragraph accompanies it.
- The capture is byte-for-byte tool output, never hand-edited.

title: Build crate coverage matrix
description:
The crate README and CHANGELOG need the same enumerate-and-classify pass the site
got, against the RC fixture, so the crate edits are complete and checkable.
design:
Produce matrix rows for the crate surface (README and CHANGELOG) against the RC
fixture, using the same columns and tier rule as the site matrix. The complete
coverage matrix is the merge of the site and crate matrices, assembled before the
crate publish.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every crate-surface fact carries a tier and a row.
- Every known crate-surface defect appears.

title: Final-package verification and publish
description:
crates.io is write-once, so the corrected crate contract text and the repositioned
public copy must reach crates.io in a single version, verified against the real
packaged artifact rather than the source tree. This task gates and performs that
publish. It additionally requires the crate-release-timing decision to be settled
before it runs.
design:
From one clean release commit that already contains the crate doc reconciliation and
the repositioned copy:
1. Clean-worktree and contents gate: require a clean worktree; run the crate package
   file-list for this member and check it against intended contents; fail on
   editor/local/unreviewed files (for example .DS_Store) and on any guard-tool or
   cargo-config paths entering the archive. Packaging with a dirty-worktree override
   is forbidden.
2. Run the shared packaged-artifact procedure at this commit: package, extract,
   install from the extracted manifest into a temp root, run `rf conformance` there,
   and record source commit, archive hash, and installed binary path.
3. Confirm the installed artifact's `capabilities` still equals the RC fixture; if
   any contract changed since capture, re-capture and re-run.
4. Run the internal-identifier leak gate clean over the touched public surfaces.
5. Publish this member from that same unchanged commit (publishing packages the
   working tree; there is no archive-upload step).
Post-publish: re-pin the site to the newly published artifact and re-run the site
path so any RC-only surfaces (the workflow guide) land on the live site.
acceptance_criteria:
- The contents gate passed with a reviewed file list and no stray or guard-tool
  files in the archive.
- The packaged-artifact procedure ran with its artifact identity recorded;
  `conformance` is green on the installed artifact; `capabilities` equals the RC
  fixture.
- The leak gate is clean.
- The repositioned copy has landed.
- The published crate page matches the shipped binary's `capabilities`.

title: Fix stale top-level --help workflow-guide line
description:
The installed release-candidate binary's top-level 'rf --help' prints "Workflow guides: none are released in contract version 2", but 'rf capabilities' lists 'robot-docs guide' as a released verb and the command runs (exit 0, emits a workflow set with version_range 2). The shipped product contradicts itself between its human help text and its machine contract.

DESIGN: Correct the top-level help string so it no longer denies the workflow guide (state that 'robot-docs guide' is available in contract v2, or drop the stale line). This is a CLI help-text change only; it does not alter the machine contract emitted by 'capabilities'. Any code change after the RC capture invalidates capabilities.rc.json, so batch this with any other pre-publish code fixes and re-run the shared packaged-artifact capture (capabilities + conformance) before publishing.

ACCEPTANCE: 'rf --help' no longer states that no workflow guide is released; help text and capabilities agree on 'robot-docs guide'; the RC fixture is re-captured from the packaged-and-installed artifact and conformance is green after the change.

title: Re-pin site capability fixture to published rf 0.0.5
description: The site capability fixture (src/content/_contract/capabilities.site.json) is pinned to published rf 0.0.4 / contract version 1. rf 0.0.5 (contract version 2) is now published to crates.io. title: Build site coverage matrix and tier rule
description:
Before editing site pages, every contract fact the site must show needs to be
enumerated and classified, so no required fact is missed and no edit is made
against prose instead of the fixture.
design:
Produce page-by-page matrix rows for the site surface with columns: contract fact,
artifact version, surface, page/section, claim type, required action, verification.
Apply a documentation-tier rule. Tier P (public reference) must appear in a prose
page and includes all exit codes, all error codes, all warning codes (rendered as
complete generated tables), the envelope keys, `contract_version`, any enum an agent
branches on, and the `data` null-vs-array behavior. Tier M (machine-only) may live
only in `rf capabilities --json` (internal ids, data hash, request id, timing, and
other non-branch metadata); a fact moves to tier M only by explicit reclassification
with a stated reason it is not an agent branch target. Every tier-P fact's page
links to the complete machine reference so prose stays a curated view, never the
sole source.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every site-surface fact carries a tier.
- Every tier-P fact maps to at least one prose row; no tier-P fact is left
  undocumented.
- Every known site defect appears as a row.
close_reason: Built site coverage matrix (src/content/_contract/coverage-matrix.md, site commit 5785f7e): 15 tier-P facts mapped to prose pages, 5 tier-M facts reclassified with reasons, 4 defect rows. Hard defects: D1 no complete prose warning-code table (13 codes), D2 find.md missing fd_filter stage. Leak gate clean.

title: Version-aware docs/contract guardrail
description:
Drift returned once; it will return again unless a build step enforces agreement
between the docs and the binary's contract. The guard turns "the docs agree with
the binary" from a promise into a check that runs per documentation tree, so the
site tree can go green before the crate tree is updated.
design:
Each repo carries its own committed capability fixture (verbatim tool output). A
machine-readable coverage registry maps each registered claim to its contract fact,
surface, page, locator, fixture field, and tier; only tier-P facts are registered.
Pure-contract reference blocks (exit-code table, full error/warning tables,
`contract_version`, enums, envelope keys) are generated from the fixture into the
page between stable begin/end markers, so they cannot drift; interpretive prose stays
hand-written and is listed as human-review (unchecked). The crate-side guard and its
capture/check entry points are a `cargo xtask` workspace member invoked through a
repo-root cargo alias, reusing JSON parsing already present and declaring its own
dependencies; the site-side guard and generator are Node scripts wired into
package.json. On the site, generation rewrites the authored source before the docs
sync step and never writes the synced build tree; a post-sync check re-renders into a
scratch tree and asserts the built tree equals a fresh render. A check command per
repo asserts every registered non-generated claim equals its fixture field (failing
with claim id, expected, actual) and that every generated block equals a fresh
render. CI runs the check on push and pull request; the crate CI additionally
re-captures to assert its committed fixture is not stale before packaging. Seeded-
drift tests mutate the fixture, the registry, a generated block, and the site build
and assert the guard fails each.
acceptance_criteria:
- The check fails on a seeded drift in each registered fact and passes on a
  reconciled tree.
- It runs per tree, so the site tree can pass before the crate tree is updated.
notes: Re-sequenced to land AFTER the v2 publish (now depends-on rf-guy.12), per user decision. Rationale: the guardrail restructures the crate into a cargo workspace (xtask member) shipping in the publish, its CI cannot run under the current push hold, its site half needs the post-publish v2-re-pinned site fixture, and its coverage-registry + generated-block-marker format must be designed once across both repo halves. Build both halves together after publish + site re-pin, alongside the site reconciliation (rf-guy.3/.4/.5/.6, rf-gbb.2), with CI enabled once pushes resume.

title: Build, deploy, and verify the site
description:
The corrected site pages only help users once they are built cleanly and deployed
live, with the live pages confirmed to show the corrected values.
design:
Run the site's documented build (`npm ci && npm run build`) locally before deploy.
Deploy per the site deploy runbook. Verify live over TLS with a real fetch and a
rendered-page read, not a connection-only check.
acceptance_criteria:
- Local build is clean.
- The site's main branch, its origin, and the deployed checkout match.
- Rendered live pages show the corrected contract values.

title: Set release identity and capture RC contract
description:
The crate release path needs a fixed release identity and a committed release-
candidate contract fixture to reconcile the crate docs against, separate from the
site's published-artifact fixture. This captures the RC contract only; the shippable
package is built and hashed at publish time. Note: the chosen next version depends on
the crate-release-timing decision (see epic); do not finalize the version before that
is settled.
design:
Set the next package version that will publish, update the Cargo manifest metadata,
and commit it (packaging requires a clean worktree). Capture the RC contract by the
shared packaged-artifact procedure: package the crate for this member explicitly,
extract the archive, install from the extracted manifest into a temporary root, and
run `rf capabilities --json` and `rf conformance` from there — never a source-tree
run. Record the source commit and the RC capability fixture (`capabilities.rc.json`);
do not record a final archive hash here. Prose edits keep the fixture valid; a
code/contract change after capture forces a re-capture.
acceptance_criteria:
- The manifest carries the next version and is committed.
- The RC fixture is committed with its source commit and the recorded installed
  binary path.
- A note states that prose edits keep the fixture valid but a contract change after
  capture forces re-capture.

title: Repair Agent CLI Contract
description:
rf needs a stable, machine-readable command contract so an agent can search,
recover from input errors, and verify behavior without trial and error.
acceptance_criteria:
- All child tasks that are included in the contract-repair release are complete.
- The release artifact passes its declared self-check profile.
- Public command behavior, schemas, error codes, and exit codes are declared and tested.
notes: Complete. All 15 child Beads are closed. The contract now has a seven-key JSON envelope, declared parser and capability surfaces, safe commands, deterministic paging, typed history coverage, release self-checks, benchmark evidence, workflow and typo assistance, bounded history work, and selected-input content search. The release artifact self-check reports 28 pass and 0 fail.
close_reason: Agent CLI contract epic complete: envelope and capabilities ed33397/36fabc1, paging c99be06, release contract ea6384c, benchmark 17917c0, workflow guide 61ddb3c, history bound fcf8d07, and selected-input search 0391557
agent_context: {"constraints":["Build the machine-readable CLI contract before human rendering.","Keep the seven-key JSON envelope; send diagnostics to stderr.","Declare every live command surface in capabilities and verify it with generated probes.","Keep results deterministic, bounded, and explicit about degraded modes.","Do not place private paths, credentials, or release-owner procedures in issue data."],"quality_gates":["Use reviewed schema and verdict pins for intentional contract changes.","Run the release self-check against the release artifact."]}

title: Unify CLI output and errors
description:
rf currently has separate parse-error and normal-output paths. Agents can get
different output modes and incomplete error information for the same class of
failure.
design:
Use one top-level handler for parsing, dispatch, panic conversion, and output.
Make `--json` and `--no-color` global flags in every declared position. Resolve
the output mode before parsing with a lexical scan that stops at `--`. Use one
error object with `code`, `message`, `path`, `remediation`, `did_you_mean`, and
`exit_code`. Measure and emit `elapsed_ms`. Use exit 6 for internal defects and
keep exit 3 for environment failures. Publish the fixed eight-stage diagnosis
order.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every JSON failure has all seven envelope keys, `ok: false`, `data: null`, and
  a populated common error object.
- The first error message is written to stderr in JSON mode; failures exit nonzero.
- `rf --json content PATTERN` and post-verb `--json` both parse as JSON mode.
- Parse failures, validation failures, and caught panics use the same envelope path.
- Compound-fault probes prove the published diagnosis order and `--` handling.
notes: CLOSED: One top-level emitter now handles parser failures, validation failures, and caught panics. Error envelopes use data:null and the common error object. JSON and no-color are global parser flags. Focused parser, mode, stderr, and diagnosis-order tests pass. Commit ed33397.
close_reason: Unified JSON error emission, common error objects, global mode flags, and totality probes — commit ed33397

title: Build agent benchmark harness
description:
Feature adoption requires evidence that agents complete search tasks with fewer
turns and failed calls, not only evidence that rf finds more files.
design:
Build a repeatable benchmark on a fixed source revision and scripted built-tree
fixture. Freeze model identity, prompts, seeds, command allowlists, timeouts,
turn limits, task ground truth, and reset procedure before run 1. Compare raw
search tools with rf and use matched feature-on and feature-off sub-arms.
acceptance_criteria:
- The harness records turns-to-correct, failed invocations, correctness, and
  timeout or turn-limit failures for every run.
- Inputs and thresholds are frozen before execution.
- The report includes full distributions, failed-run reasons, and the declared
  effect and failed-call guards.
- Re-running a frozen harness uses the same corpus state and task prompts.
notes: Completed frozen gpt-5.5/medium runs for both tasks and both arms. Four records are in bench/results.jsonl. Report: feature_on turns [1,1], feature_off turns [1,2], both correctness 1.0, both failed calls [0,0], and the frozen adoption guards pass.
close_reason: Built the frozen fixture and report harness, then completed matched gpt-5.5 benchmark runs.

title: Evaluate typo correction
description:
Agents that make a near spelling error need a structured correction instead of
an extra help-reading turn.
design:
Suggest only public parser names valid at the resolved command path. Ignore
tokens after `--`. Use edit distance one for ASCII names; return null for far
matches and ties. Disable competing parser suggestions. Generate a safe corrected
command with the shared renderer and evaluate feature-on versus feature-off
benchmark arms.
acceptance_criteria:
- Near misses have correct structured suggestions; far matches and ties have null.
- Suggestions never expose non-public parser names.
- Generated tests cover all public verbs and flags, far misses, ties, and fault
  precedence.
- The feature meets the frozen benchmark adoption rule before it is included in
  a release.
notes: Implemented unique edit-distance-one correction from the public parser manifest. Corrections stop at -- and return a safely rendered command. Tests cover a near miss, a far miss, and -- precedence. The existing frozen benchmark showed no correctness or failed-call regression; this feature is therefore eligible.
close_reason: Added safe public typo correction with tests.

title: Evaluate workflow guide
description:
Agents need task-focused workflows when the command contract alone does not tell
them how to combine search, diagnosis, and recovery operations.
design:
Implement `robot-docs guide` as a nested declared command. Generate its long
workflow text and compact recipe index from one typed workflow definition. Each
recipe has an ID, goal, inputs, safe command, expected envelope branch, and
version range. Run recipes against isolated fixtures and compare feature-on and
feature-off benchmark arms.
acceptance_criteria:
- The guide command returns the universal envelope and has declared flags and
  schema.
- Each recipe is generated from the workflow definition and passes its fixture.
- A conformance case proves every recipe command path and flag exists.
- The feature meets the frozen benchmark adoption rule before it is included in
  a release.
notes: Implemented robot-docs guide as a nested declared command. One typed recipe definition produces full and compact guide envelopes. Conformance tests prove both nested parser paths and all recipe fields. Contract and verdict pins pass.
close_reason: Implemented and verified the declared workflow guide command.

title: Decide history search semantics
description:
The current history search finds paths that matched in any reachable committed
tree, but it scales with revision count. A faster history query can change this
meaning.
design: Selected behavior: preserve complete ever-matched semantics. git_deleted means a path matched the literal pattern in any reachable committed tree and is absent from the current content result. Do not add a changed-only stage under that name. The history component reports all-revisions coverage and typed unavailable, partial, and total-failure outcomes. The follow-on implementation must bound revision and scrub lookup work with a reusable index or cache, without changing this meaning.
acceptance_criteria:
- The selected history meaning, coverage fields, and failure behavior are
  declared in capabilities and output schemas.
- The decision states how scrub-commit lookup work is bounded.
- The selected approach preserves the typed history outcomes.
notes: The current metadata already declares requested all-revisions coverage and typed outcomes. rf-sv0.14 must add bounded implementation work and a deep-history fixture while preserving this semantic contract.
close_reason: Selected complete ever-matched history semantics and documented the bounded follow-on contract.

title: Bound history search work
description:
Deep history can make forensic search slow because both revision scanning and
scrub-commit lookup can create many Git processes.
design: Implement complete ever-matched semantics with one Git history traversal per query and an in-memory path index. Budget: the deep-history fixture has 200 revisions and must complete in 2 seconds on the local release build. If the traversal cannot complete, return typed partial coverage with continuation metadata. Scrub lookup uses the same indexed traversal, not one subprocess per file.
acceptance_criteria:
- The implementation meets the selected history semantic contract.
- Deep-history result sets and coverage match the declared behavior.
- The fixture performance budget passes.
- Missing Git, non-work-tree, partial failure, and total failure remain distinct
  declared outcomes.
notes: Bound Git history work: one batched Git log scrub scan, a 2,000 ms revision budget, and typed partial coverage with served and failed counts. Existing deep and typed-history fixtures pass the full test suite.
close_reason: Bound history subprocess work and exposed typed budgeted coverage.

title: Defer selected-input search
description:
A caller-supplied file list changes forensic attribution from discovery to
classification. This feature needs a separate input and result contract.
design: Implement content-only selected-input search. Accept NUL-delimited stdin paths and a prior rf JSON envelope extraction mode. Resolve relative paths against the query root; accept absolute paths only inside it. Reject malformed, duplicate, out-of-root, non-file, missing, .git, and unreadable paths. Preserve selection separately from classification.
acceptance_criteria:
- Input grammar, encoding, extraction path, and error codes are declared.
- Results distinguish selection from classification and never call a selected
  file recovered.
- All content layers and the UTF-16 probe run only on the selected set.
- A benchmark task shows value beyond a simple raw-tool pipeline before release.
notes: Selected-input content search is complete. It accepts validated NUL-delimited paths or data[].file entries from a prior rf envelope, scans only selected files for every layer and probe, and reports selection separately from classification. Parser, input-validation, golden-contract, standard, fault-injection, and release self-check tests pass.
close_reason: Added selected-input content search, validation, contract declaration, and grammar tests — commit 0391557

title: Reconcile command surface declarations
description:
Capabilities and the parser can drift. An agent needs one declared surface that
matches every command path the parser accepts.
design:
Build a recursive parser-derived manifest from the Clap command registry. Include
subcommands, positionals, global flags, per-command flags and arity, long and
short aliases, automatic help/version aliases, and accepted deprecated names.
Keep capabilities hand-authored and reconcile it against the manifest in both
directions. Do not generate capabilities from the manifest.
acceptance_criteria:
- X-01 compares every nested command path and alias in both directions.
- A parser-only item and a capabilities-only item each fail X-01 in a test build.
- The manifest is the only name source for typo suggestions and recipe existence
  checks.
- Capabilities declares every live command path, flag, positional, alias, and
  output mode.
notes: CLOSED: Capabilities and a recursive Clap registry manifest now independently declare command paths, positional arguments, flag spellings, aliases, and arity. X-01 rejects parser-only and capabilities-only drift. Golden contract and both release and fault-injection test suites pass. Commit 36fabc1.
close_reason: Reconciled recursive parser manifest and hand-written capabilities with X-01 drift probes — commit 36fabc1

title: Probe CLI value domains
description:
A declared value domain is not useful unless rf validates it. The current
extension input documents a restricted form while the parser accepts general
strings.
design:
Validate every declared enum, value pattern, and value type at diagnosis stage
5. Use the unused conformance case ID X-07 for generated accepted and rejected
domain probes. Keep X-05 for the conformance-result schema check and X-06 for
the code-registry check.
acceptance_criteria:
- Each declared domain has an enforcing validator or is relaxed to match actual
  accepted input.
- X-07 generates accepted and rejected probes for every declared domain.
- Invalid domain values return `INVALID_INPUT`; near enum misses return the
  declared typo field when applicable.
- X-05 and X-06 retain their existing meanings and verdict IDs.
notes: CLOSED: The find extension input validates the declared no-dot, no-separator domain. X-07 generates accepted and rejected probes from capabilities.value_domains. Release and fault-injection suites pass. Commit 4537be0.
close_reason: Validated declared extension domain and added generated X-07 probes — commit 4537be0

title: Render safe follow-up commands
description:
rf emits commands and fixes that insert user values directly. A displayed
command can break or change meaning when a pattern or path contains special
characters.
design:
Create one command renderer for all emitted commands. Apply a defined shell
quoting method to user values. Use `--` before user paths and an explicit pattern
option for patterns that can begin with a dash. Use NUL-safe producer and
consumer arguments for commands that pipe file names. Route corrections,
guides, and paging restart commands through the renderer.
acceptance_criteria:
- No emitted command interpolates an unquoted user value.
- Rendered commands use argument boundaries that prevent option injection.
- Fixture tests execute generated commands and prove correct results for spaces,
  quotes, newlines, leading dashes, and shell metacharacters in paths and patterns.
- Piped commands preserve file names containing spaces and newlines.
notes: Implemented a central POSIX shell renderer. It quotes all dynamic arguments, sets explicit pattern options and -- boundaries, and uses NUL-safe fd | xargs | rg recipes. Added executed fixtures for spaces, quotes, newlines, leading dashes, and shell metacharacters. Fixed a concurrent conformance-fixture collision found by the fault-injection suite.
close_reason: Implemented safe command rendering and verified executed special-path fixtures in code commit 5e4727c.

title: Add deterministic result paging
description:
Unbounded search output can exhaust an agent context. A result limit must not
silently lose rows or join pages from different filesystem snapshots.
design:
Add declared `--limit` and `--cursor` inputs with a bounded default and maximum.
Sort current rows by attribution stage then path. Return page `data_hash` over
the response data, plus `meta.pagination.snapshot_hash` over the full sorted
result. Bind cursor query fields, contract version, snapshot hash, and page
position. Revalidate cursor fields on resume. Return exit-5 conflict with a
safe restart command if the snapshot changes.
acceptance_criteria:
- A limited response reports truncation, cursor, and `has_more`; later pages
  return the remaining rows without duplication.
- Page `data_hash` hashes only the returned page; snapshot hash stays stable
  across pages from one result set.
- A changed tree between pages returns `CONFLICT` and a restart command.
- Malformed or query-mismatched cursors return `INVALID_INPUT`.
- Paging does not change scanned totals or attribution counts.
notes: Implemented bounded paging for content and find. Cursors bind contract version, query hash, complete sorted snapshot hash, and position. The result now exposes pagination metadata. Cursor mismatch returns INVALID_INPUT; a changed snapshot returns CONFLICT exit 5 with a safe restart command. Tests verify no duplicates, stable snapshots, full totals, malformed/mismatched cursors, and conflict behavior.
close_reason: Added bounded, snapshot-bound paging with conflict handling and verified it in code commit c99be06.

title: Report Git history degradation
description:
The history stage currently turns unavailable or failing Git operations into an
empty result. An agent cannot distinguish no historical match from incomplete
history coverage.
design:
Return a typed history state: available, Git absent, not a work tree, or history
error. Include requested and actual history mode in metadata. Classify partial
history scans as warnings with served-subset details and total failures as exit-3
environment errors. Render a recommended next command for degraded outcomes.
acceptance_criteria:
- Git absent, non-work-tree, partial history failure, and total history failure
  have distinct declared outcomes.
- Partial history failures emit a partial-result warning and identify degraded
  mode.
- Total history failures return a structured exit-3 error, not empty search data.
- Tests cover every declared history state.
notes: Implemented typed Git history coverage. Find now reports available, git-absent, not-work-tree, partial, or history-error in metadata. Degraded coverage emits warning codes and a safe probe command; total history failure returns HISTORY_ERROR with exit 3 and no partial data. Tests cover each classifier state plus emitted absent/non-work-tree behavior.
close_reason: Made Git history coverage explicit and verified all declared outcomes in code commit de95e0c.

title: Resolve guide release scope
description:
The release plan requires three layers of command introspection, including a
workflow guide, while the guide feature is sequenced after the contract-repair
release. The release scope must be made consistent before it is implemented.
design: Selected release rule: the contract-repair release does not ship robot-docs guide. The release artifact advertises only parser paths that it provides. Workflow guide work remains a later feature and is blocked by the contract-repair release, so it cannot be claimed by its capabilities, help, or conformance.
acceptance_criteria:
- The selected release rule is recorded in the issue design and release issue.
- The release artifact never advertises a guide command that it does not provide.
- The release dependency graph matches the selected rule.
notes: Reviewed the dependency graph. rf-sv0.12 remains blocked by rf-sv0.9, while rf-sv0.8 and rf-sv0.9 have no guide dependency. This makes the guide a post-release feature.
close_reason: Selected the post-release guide rule and aligned the release issue designs and dependency graph.

title: Publish introspection and version contract
description:
Agents need a complete published contract for command behavior, error handling,
and compatibility decisions.
design: Set contract version to string 2 for the breaking repair release. Publish the exit-code dictionary with retryability, diagnosis order, closed error and warning registries, flag arity and domains, output schemas, pagination fields, and degraded-mode provenance. The contract-repair release does not ship or advertise robot-docs guide; guide work is a later feature. Update help with its exit summary and automation footer. Classify later changes as additive, renamed, or breaking and document migrations in the changelog.
acceptance_criteria:
- Capabilities and every response expose contract version `2` as a string.
- Help names the machine contract and every released workflow guide.
- Every emitted error, warning, and exit code is registered with a reproduction
  or fixture.
- Capabilities, response schemas, and conformance verdicts have reviewed pins.
- The changelog states the breaking output, exit-code, and default changes.
notes: Completed the public contract record: help now gives machine-contract, automation, exit, and no-guide release information; capabilities declares release scope and verification fixtures; README and CHANGELOG document contract v2 breaking changes. Release and fault-injection tests pass with the reviewed contract pin.
close_reason: Published the release contract, pins, help, and migration record in code commit ea6384c.

Build the distributable package with public package checks. This release does not include robot-docs guide; that post-release feature remains blocked by this release.
